column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/esteira-rio-bump.yml
# TAB-separated: <name>
# WHAT THIS PINS. The workflow has exactly one job, `bump`, and it is the job
# that TAGS AND PUSHES. Its whole selection turns on one context path:
#     if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'
# That is a loop-breaker, and it is load-bearing in a way the YAML does not
# say out loud. The job's own final step configures git as
# `github-actions[bot]` and pushes a tag with BOT_PAT specifically SO THAT
# downstream workflows trigger (a GITHUB_TOKEN-pushed tag does not). A lane
# built to make its own pushes retrigger things needs one guard stopping it
# from retriggering ITSELF, and this `if:` is that guard, alone.
# The failure this table exists to make loud: if that condition ever inverts,
# widens, or is rewritten as an allow-list, the run still reports SUCCESS.
# A bump that correctly declines to run and a bump that can NEVER run are the
# same green tick without an assertion — which is exactly the graphql-synthesizer
# shape that put job-selection-lint in the fleet.
# THE PUBLISH AXIS (do-it / don't-do-it), stated because this job pushes:
#   row 1 `human-push-tags-and-pushes`  = the DO-IT case, and it is intended.
#   row 2 `bot-rerun-is-the-loop-breaker` = the DON'T-DO-IT case, and it is
#          intended. A self-triggered rerun must NOT cut a second tag.
# Rows 3 and 4 are the boundary rows that would otherwise rot silently:
#   row 3 proves the guard is an EXACT-MATCH DENY of one identity, not a
#         "no bots" rule — dependabot[bot] and every other bot DO bump here.
#         Someone tightening this to a substring/`contains()` test would
#         change fleet behaviour with no red anywhere; this row goes NOT-RUN.
#   row 4 proves the guard FAILS OPEN. An unresolved/empty actor bumps. That
#         is the property that flips if the condition is ever rewritten as an
#         allow-list (`github.actor == '...'`), which would look like a
#         hardening and would silently make the lane never bump again.
# `github.actor` is the ONLY context path any condition in this workflow reads,
# so it is the only key any row declares. `runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}` and
# the three `workflow_call` inputs are not job conditions and are out of scope.
# NOT ASSERTABLE HERE, on purpose: the skip-paths gate and the bump-type
# dispatch (patch/minor/major) live in STEP conditions
# (`steps.changes.outputs.skip == 'false'`) and in shell inside the steps.
# job-selection-lint asserts job selection only, so "bump ran but deliberately
# cut no tag" and "bump ran and cut a tag" are the same verdict at this
# granularity. That is the same silence one level down, and it needs a
# different layer — do not fake it with a context key here.
human-push-tags-and-pushes
# THE LOOP-BREAKER. The one case where the tagging job must not select.
bot-rerun-is-the-loop-breaker
# The guard denies ONE identity, not bots in general.
other-bot-still-bumps
# Fail-open: an unresolved actor still bumps. An allow-list rewrite breaks this.
unresolved-actor-fails-open
